# Recovering a Markov generator from stationary barrier-intervention snapshots

4 November 2026. Research theorem draft, pending independent audit and literature-priority review. This is an exact identifiability result under strong controls, not a demonstrated instrument, a universal inference method, or a claim of a civilisation-changing capability. No Python used.

## 1. Model and operational assumptions

Let W be an irreducible continuous-time Markov generator on n≥3 fully observed, correctly specified states, in the column convention dp/dt=Wp. Thus 1ᵀW=0, off-diagonal W_ij≥0, and Wπ=0 for a unique positive normalized stationary distribution π. Let G be a known simple connected undirected graph whose edges each carry strictly positive rates in both directions. There are no unobserved parallel channels in the interpretation of thermodynamic currents.

For an oriented edge e=(a,b), define b_e=e_b−e_a, u_e=W_ba e_a−W_ab e_b and current j_e=u_eᵀπ. A barrier intervention multiplies both directed rates on just this edge by the same factor t_e>0, t_e≠1, leaving every other off-diagonal rate unchanged and maintaining column sums. Therefore

W^(e)=W+(t_e−1)b_e u_eᵀ.

Observe only π and the stationary distribution π^(e) of each intervened generator. Set d_e=π^(e)−π. The factors t_e need not be calibrated or even equal across experiments. Locality to the claimed edge, nontriviality, and stability of the state space are indispensable controls for the stated setup. Equal scaling in the two directions is required for the symmetric-barrier interpretation and the current-zero equivalence below, not for the inverse-ray uniqueness algebra; Section 11 explicitly relaxes it. This is not merely an arbitrary state-potential perturbation.

Assume the observed nonzero-current intervention edges contain a spanning subgraph E_* with connected cycle matroid: every two edges can be linked through a sequence of simple cycles with shared edges. A familiar sufficient case is a simple biconnected graph with nonzero stationary current on every edge. A single n-cycle with nonzero circulation satisfies the assumption. It is sufficient to use this spanning active subgraph, even if other unperturbed edges exist in the generator.

## Verdict and scope

The stated exact identifiability theorem, finite-control consistency test, and conditional statistical bound pass this independent algebraic review. No counterexample was found under the declared assumptions. This is not a certification of novelty, physical realizability, experimental advantage, or general hidden-state inference. The proof's opening “pending independent audit” status is superseded by this companion audit; literature priority remains unresolved.

The distinction between a sufficient topology for the physical inverse problem and a necessary topology for its unrestricted linear ray equations is important. A positive generator and matching response rays do not alone certify the claimed finite symmetric controls. These qualifications were communicated to the author and the finite-control check and broader edge-local interpretation were incorporated before the reviewed version was frozen.

## 1. Response identity, signs and directed rates

With column generators and b=e_b−e_a, the edge contribution b uᵀ has exactly the required two off-diagonal entries and their negative diagonal compensators. Subtracting stationary equations gives Wd=−(t−1)(uᵀπ')b, with the sign as written. W restricted to H={1ᵀx=0} is invertible because its sole nullvector is the normalized positive π, outside H. A zero response is equivalent to zero baseline edge current for a nonunit symmetric intervention. A nonzero response cannot have a vanishing coefficient in this identity.

For candidate V, A=V_H W_H^−1 preserves every measured incidence ray. Cycle dependencies force its eigenvalues to agree; connectivity through shared cycles propagates this equality. Spanning then implies A=cI. Conservation and Vπ=0 extend this identity to all of Rⁿ. This reasoning does not require V_H to be invertible. Consequently the unrestricted homogeneous reconstruction really has a one-dimensional nullspace, not merely uniqueness among nonsingular candidates. Positive off-diagonal rates force c>0. The procedure therefore recovers the two directed rates separately up to a common positive clock, rather than merely their sum or unoriented currents. Trace normalization only chooses units.

# Correction: direct endpoint recovery by a classical maximum principle

4 November 2026. This corrects the significance and acquisition mechanism of the earlier blind stationary tomography packet. Its theorem remains valid, but its graphic-matroid reconstruction is unnecessary. A simpler same-data operation also weakens the sufficient graph assumption from 3-vertex-connectivity to biconnectivity. The maximum principle itself is established mathematics, with directly relevant stationary-response prior below. No priority claim is made for its inverse-problem application.

## 1. Exact operation and proof

Use the column convention for an irreducible finite Markov generator W: off-diagonal entries are nonnegative, 1ᵀW=0, and Wπ=0 with π>0. An intervention changes only the two directed rates on {a,b}; symmetric multiplication of those rates by an unknown positive factor is a special case. Let π′ be its stationary distribution and d=π′−π. Assume d≠0. Subtracting stationarity gives

W d = α(e_b−e_a), with α≠0.

Define h_i=d_i/π_i and L=W diag(π). Since L1=0, at every state i,

(Lh)_i = Σ_(j≠i) W_ij π_j (h_j−h_i).

Thus h is harmonic at every nontarget state. Assume, for this pair, that the baseline positive-rate support contains a spanning bidirected graph which remains connected after deleting either a or b. A spanning biconnected bidirected graph suffices simultaneously for every target pair.

Reverse the names a,b if necessary so α>0. At b the displayed sum is positive, so b cannot maximize h. At a it is negative, so a cannot minimize h. If a nontarget i maximized h, its harmonic equation, a sum of nonpositive terms with positive coefficients along bidirected edges, would force every neighboring value to equal that maximum. Propagate along a path from i to b avoiding a. All internal vertices are nontargets, so b would also maximize h, a contradiction. The analogous argument along a path avoiding b excludes a nontarget minimum. Hence

argmax_i h_i = a, and argmin_i h_i = b,

uniquely. Their unordered pair is the intervention target, regardless of its unknown amplitude or sign. Computing π′_i/π_i gives exactly the same extrema. This uses the measured state names directly and needs no graph reconstruction or row-permutation alignment.
